title: Delhi High Court, Airport Among Six Locations to Receive Bomb Threats on Independence Day Eve
excerpt: Security agencies deployed bomb squads and sniffer dogs across the national capital after email-based bomb threats targeted multiple locations, a day before India celebrates its 79th Independence Day.
body:
• Delhi High Court, IGI Airport, and four other locations in the national capital received bomb threats via email on August 14, a day before Independence Day
  • Security agencies deployed bomb disposal squads and sniffer dogs across all targeted sites as part of heightened pre-Independence Day protocols
  • India has seen a surge in email-based bomb threats targeting courts, airports, and schools over the past year, with most turning out to be hoaxes

Multiple locations across New Delhi, including the Delhi High Court and Indira Gandhi International Airport, received bomb threats via email on Thursday, August 14, sending security agencies into high alert just hours before the country celebrates its 79th Independence Day.

According to reports from NDTV and India Today, bomb threats were reported at six locations in the national capital. The Delhi High Court and IGI Airport were among the primary targets, along with four other sites. Delhi Police immediately activated standard operating procedures, deploying bomb disposal squads, sniffer dog units, and fire services personnel to all affected locations.

Security Response and Heightened Alert

The threats come at a time when security across India is already at peak levels ahead of the Independence Day celebrations on August 15. The Red Fort, where the Prime Minister traditionally delivers the national address, is under multi-layered security cover.

Delhi Police cordoned off the affected areas and launched systematic searches. At the High Court, proceedings were disrupted as judges, lawyers, and staff were alerted to the threat. Bomb detection teams conducted floor-by-floor sweeps of the court complex. At IGI Airport, the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) ramped up screening procedures and activated the Bomb Threat Assessment Committee (BTAC).

"As per the SOP, bomb detection teams and the dog squad are inside. We are carrying out search operations."

— Delhi Police spokesperson

Pattern of Email-Based Bomb Threats

The incident follows a troubling pattern of email-based bomb threats that has gripped Indian cities over the past year. In September 2025, both the Delhi and Bombay High Courts received similar threatening emails on the same day, forcing evacuations and suspending proceedings. In October 2025, over 300 schools in Delhi and several airports received coordinated hoax bomb threats from a group identifying itself as "Terrorizers111."

In most cases, authorities have traced the emails to anonymous or spoofed accounts, often routed through VPNs, making identification of the senders difficult. Cybercrime units across multiple states are investigating what appears to be a coordinated campaign to create panic.

Independence Day Security Measures

The threats have prompted authorities to further tighten the already extensive security arrangements for Independence Day. Delhi Police, along with paramilitary forces, intelligence agencies, and the National Security Guard, have established a comprehensive security umbrella across the capital.

Anti-drone systems, sharpshooters, and CCTV surveillance have been deployed at key locations. Police have also increased foot patrols and vehicle checks across the city, with particular attention to crowded areas, government buildings, and transport hubs.

Authorities have urged citizens to remain vigilant and report any suspicious activity or unattended objects immediately. While past bomb threats of this nature have largely been declared hoaxes after investigation, security agencies have maintained that every threat is treated with full seriousness until cleared.
nri_angle: Bomb threats at major Indian landmarks ahead of Independence Day are closely watched by the Indian diaspora, particularly those planning travel to India during the festive period.
